children.label: retrieval.py
children.summary: SearchHit, IndexedDocument, RetrievedDocument
children.details: `SearchHit` is one embedded text with its cosine `distance`. `IndexedDocument` is an entry in the BM25 index. `RetrievedDocument` is the pipeline output: reciprocal-rank-fusion `score`, `ranks` per ranking, best chunk `position` and `text`, `title` and an optional `rerank_score`.

outline.name: SearchHit
outline.doc: One embedded text found for a query, closest first by cosine distance.

outline.name: IndexedDocument
outline.doc: A document in a keyword (BM25) index, in index order.

outline.name: RetrievedDocument
outline.doc:
A document found for a query by the retrieval pipeline, best first.

`score` is the document's reciprocal rank fusion score; `ranks` holds its rank in each
ranking that found it (1 is the top), keyed by ranking name. `position` and `text` are
its best chunk, or its first chunk when only keyword search found it. `rerank_score`
is the reranker's relevance score, None when the pipeline ran without a reranker.

children.label: Dynamic tables
children.summary: Table factory: source_table builds one SQLModel table per (vector size, source type) from a shared column base.
children.details: `source_table` builds each table with `types.new_class` from a shared base and sets `__tablename__` to `<source>_<suffix>`; the class name is derived from the source and the base class name. Splitting by source keeps each DiskANN index small and lets retrieval search sources separately; splitting by vector size is needed because a pgvector column has a fixed dimension. `EMBEDDING_TABLES` is built at import time for every `SourceType`, so all tables are registered before `create_tables` runs.

children.label: Evaluation runs
children.summary: Evaluation runs and per-question results.
children.details:
Two tables. `eval_runs` (`EvalRunRecord`): `dataset`, `system`, `judge`, `question_count`, `started_at`, `finished_at` and a JSONB `summary` holding the `RunSummary` once finished. `eval_results` (`EvalResultRecord`): one row per question per run, with `run_id` FK, `question_id`, `question_type`, `answer`, `retrieved_doc_ids` and `cited_doc_ids` (JSONB), `document_recall`, `extra_docs`, `correct`, `completeness`, `score`, `facts_covered`, `judge_reasoning`, `error` and `trace` (JSONB list of `TraceStep`).

Writer: `evaluation/pipeline.py` (`create_run`, `add_results`, `finish_run`). Readers: `evaluate.py` (`wrong_question_ids`), run listings (`list_runs`, `results_of_run`).

Score is correctness times completeness (0 if wrong, None if not graded).

children.summary: TraceStep, SystemAnswer, AnswerGrade, QuestionResult

outline.name: TraceStep
SystemAnswer
outline.doc:
What a RAG system returns for one question.

Its answer, the documents it retrieved, and, for systems that record them, the
documents its answer cites and the steps it took.

outline.doc:
A judge's verdict on one answer against the gold answer and its facts.

`facts_covered` has one entry per answer fact of the question, in order. Field order
matters: a judge filling this schema writes its reasoning before the verdict.

Share of the answer facts the answer covers.

Returns:

outline.doc: The evaluation of one question: retrieval metrics, the grade, or the error.

outline.name: MetricSummary
outline.doc:
Benchmark metrics averaged over a set of questions.

`document_recall` averages only questions that expect documents; it is None when
none of them do (high-level and info-not-found questions).

outline.name: RunSummary
outline.doc: Metrics of a whole run, overall and per question type.

outline.name: RetrievalMetrics
outline.doc:
Retrieval quality over a set of questions that expect documents.

`recall_at` maps k to the mean share of expected documents among the top k hits.
`reachable` is the mean share of expected documents that are in the index at all:
the best recall any k could reach.

children.label: Pipeline runs
children.summary: Run progress and timing for the progress page.
children.details:
Table `pipeline_runs` (`PipelineRunRecord`) tracks one run of a pipeline or evaluation: `pipeline`, `stage`, `status` (`running`, finished, ...), `unit`, `total_items` / `done_items`, optional `total_chars` / `done_chars` (BigInteger), `note`, `started_at`, `updated_at`.

Writer: `progress/recorder.py` (`start_run`, `update_run` after every batch). Reader: `progress/page.py` through `latest_run_state`, which returns `RunState` with elapsed time and estimated time left.

The ETA assumes average speed so far, in characters per second when the run counts characters and in items per second otherwise. A run still `running` whose `updated_at` is older than `STALE_AFTER` is reported as `stopped`, which is how killed runs are detected.

children.label: pipeline_run.py

outline.name: PipelineRunRecord
outline.doc:
One run of a pipeline or an evaluation, updated after every batch.

`total_items` is what this run had left when it started, counted in `unit` (e.g.
documents or questions); `done_items` counts what it has finished since. The
characters are optional (0 when a run doesn't weigh its items by size); when set, the
time left is estimated from them. `stage` names the step it is on, and `note` holds
any extra line for the page, such as the money spent so far. `status` is `running`
until the run ends; a run that was killed stays `running` but stops updating
`updated_at`.

children.label: Replace and load
children.summary: Replace-by-tool: each replace_* call overwrites what that tool stored earlier, then load_* returns a dict keyed by document id.
children.details: Each `replace_*` function deletes all rows whose `method` equals the given tool name, then inserts the new rows and commits. A rerun of one experiment therefore replaces only its own output, while the `unique` `document_id` constraint means only one method's row can exist per document at a time. `load_*` returns dicts keyed by document id, so callers look up by `documents.id`.

children.label: Model, table, repository
children.summary: Three layers per entity: pydantic model in models/, SQLModel table in tables/, plain query functions in repository/ taking a Session.
children.details: Every entity follows the same three-layer layout, so to find how something is stored look for the same file name in all three folders. Example: `question` has `models/question.py` (`Question`), `tables/question.py` (`QuestionRecord`) and `repository/question.py` (`insert_questions`, `load_questions`, `to_question`). Repository functions take a `Session` (or `AsyncSession` in `search.py`), return pydantic models or records, and callers decide transaction scope; some commit (`replace_*`), others explicitly do not (`insert_embeddings`, `upsert_parsed_documents`, `store_chunks`).

children.label: Shared helpers
children.summary: Two small helpers: the central prompt store and the seeded benchmark sample.
children.details:
Cross-cutting helpers imported by the evaluation and indexing code rather than a pipeline of their own.

- `prompts.py` serves every LLM prompt from `prompts.yaml` (judge, answer, agent and tool descriptions), used by `evaluation/judge.py`, `agent.py`, `pipeline_answer.py` and `summary_search.py`.
- `sampling.py` builds the small test corpus: all documents cited by benchmark questions plus a fixed number of seeded random distractors. It is called by `index_bm25.py` and `pipelines/data_ingestion.py` when a `sample` size is given.

Read `prompts.py` first (30 lines), then `sampling.py`.

children.label: Files
children.summary: The two helper files: prompt store and corpus sampler.
children.details: Both files are tiny, stateless and have no CLI. They depend only on `prompts.yaml` and the repository layer, so any module can import them without cycles.

children.label: prompts.py
children.summary: load_prompts() reads prompts.yaml once; prompt(name, **values) fills placeholders.
children.details:
`load_prompts()` is `@cache`d: it reads `prompts.yaml` once and collapses single newlines into spaces with the `WRAPPED_LINE` regex, keeping blank lines as paragraph breaks.

`prompt(name, **values)` looks up a prompt and fills `{placeholders}` with `str.format`; a missing name or value raises `KeyError`. Callers typically fill them at import time, e.g. `prompt("document_answer_instructions", not_found=NOT_FOUND_ANSWER)`.

outline.name: load_prompts
outline.doc:
Read every prompt from the file, once, joining wrapped lines into paragraphs.

Returns:
    Prompt texts keyed by name.

outline.name: prompt
outline.doc:
Get one prompt with its placeholders filled in.

Args:
    name: Key of the prompt in `prompts.yaml`.
    **values: Values for the prompt's `{placeholders}`.

Returns:

Raises:
    KeyError: If there is no prompt with this name, or a placeholder has no value.

children.label: One prompt file
children.summary: All LLM prompts live in prompts.yaml; wrapped lines are joined so the file reads well.
children.details: Keeping every prompt in `prompts.yaml` lets you edit and compare wording without touching Python. Long prompts are wrapped in the YAML for readability; `load_prompts` joins those wrapped lines back into single paragraphs (blank lines stay as breaks), so the model sees clean text.

children.label: Cached loader
children.summary: @cache on load_prompts parses the YAML once; str.format fills placeholders and raises KeyError if missing.
children.details: `@cache` on `load_prompts` means the YAML is parsed once per process. `prompt()` uses `str.format`, so a missing placeholder value raises `KeyError` at call time, which surfaces typos early since most callers fill prompts at module import.

children.label: sampling.py
children.summary: sample_documents() picks all cited documents plus seeded random distractors.
children.details:
`sample_documents(session, dataset, distractors)` returns a set of document row ids. It collects `expected_doc_ids` from every question via `load_questions`, maps them to row ids with `ids_of_doc_ids`, and unions them with `sample_document_ids(..., distractors, SAMPLE_SEED)`.

Cited documents guarantee every question stays answerable; distractors make retrieval non-trivial. The constant `SAMPLE_SEED = "chunk-sample"` makes the pick deterministic.

outline.name: sample_documents
outline.signature: (session: Session, dataset: str, distractors: int) -> set[int]
outline.doc:
Pick every document a benchmark question cites, plus random other documents.

The same seed always picks the same documents, so every retrieval method indexed on
the sample searches the same corpus and their recall can be compared.

Args:
    session: Active database session.
    dataset: Dataset to sample from.
    distractors: Number of random documents added to the cited ones.

Returns:
    The row ids of the sample.

children.label: Fixed seed
children.summary: A constant seed gives the same corpus every run, so retrieval methods compare on equal ground.
children.details: `SAMPLE_SEED = "chunk-sample"` is passed to `sample_document_ids`, so the same distractors are chosen on every run. Every retrieval method indexed on the sample then searches the same corpus and their recall is comparable (see the docstring of `sample_documents`).
